From: Amelia Rivera <amelia@novacorp.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: MSA primer and party sheet

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the quick intro last week. Our legal team asked me to get the contracting materials over so we can start an internal review. Attached is our standard MSA (Vendor_MSA_v0.pdf) and a short procurement checklist the buyer needs for PO processing.

Could you do two things for us:

1) Share Redwood's MSA template and a simple party/contact sheet (billing addr, remit info, PO contact, primary technical contact, security contacts).
2) Confirm the preferred redline process (tracked changes preferred? DocuSign or Word exchange?) and a rough internal SLA for initial comments.

Procurement also flagged SOC 2 evidence and a short note on data residency — if you can point me to the right artifact or confirm region, that would speed our side up.

We have a tentative go-live window for late September; a one-week turn for initial redlines would be ideal.

Attaching: Vendor_MSA_v0.pdf (redlines expected)

Appreciate it — I can hop on a quick 30m call if helpful.

Best,
Amelia Rivera
Head of IT Procurement
NovaCorp
amelia@novacorp.com

Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 10:05:00 -0700

Hi Amelia —

Thanks for the MSA and the checklist. Leaving a couple of notes inline, but to get the process moving I've attached:
- Redwood_MSA_v1.docx (our template, tracked changes preferred)
- Party_Details_Template.xlsx (simple sheet to capture billing and technical contacts)

Redline process we prefer: Word with tracked changes for the MSA, then DocuSign for final signatures. If NovaCorp needs to use native Word comments first, that's fine — we can consolidate.

Turnaround: we typically aim for internal legal to produce an initial draft with comments within 3–5 business days for new logos; since you mentioned late September, a 1-week window for initial redlines works on our side if we get the party sheet and any immediate security asks (SOC 2 link or evidence) today.

Proposed next steps:
- Amelia: complete the Party_Details_Template.xlsx and send Vendor redline file back
- Marissa/Legal: internal review and return tracked changes by EOD Aug 24 (target)
- If there are material changes to indemnity/data/limits we can schedule a short call with legal stakeholders

Would you be available for a 30m sync on Thu 8/20 at 9am PT? If not, suggest a time.

Attachments: Redwood_MSA_v1.docx, Party_Details_Template.xlsx

Thanks —

Marissa —

Thanks, got the template and party sheet. Vendor legal also returned a marked-up draft (attached: Vendor_MSA_with_comments.docx). A few notes from our side:

- Procurement will need SOC 2 Type II report and a short confirmation of where Redwood will store customer data (we're evaluating Eu vs US residency for this product).
- Our legal is likely to ask for tighter liability language and an explicit carveout for breach remediation timelines.
- We prefer to exchange Word tracked changes first; once both parties agree, we'll move to DocuSign.

I'll complete the Party_Details_Template and send back by EOB today. Let's tentatively plan for your internal comments by Aug 24. If your legal wants to pick a few top-line items to call out in advance (liability cap, indemnity, data processing addendum, termination for convenience), that will help our negotiators focus.

Also, can you add an SSO onboarding contact? Our security team will request console access for a small set of users for testing.

Best,
Amelia

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 13:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA primer and party sheet

Marissa / Karthik —

Quick internal note from Legal after a skim of the vendor redline and your template exchange: please prioritize the following in our initial pass (we will own the tracked-changes return unless you want to do a joint session):

1) Liability & cap language — propose $1M cap for commercial accounts; escalate to me if vendor insists on unlimited liability or expressive carveouts.
2) Indemnity — narrow to third-party IP claims only; remove open-ended broad indemnities.
3) Data processing & residency — confirm product stores customer data in US by default; if NovaCorp needs EU residency we will document options but expect pricing impact.
4) SLA & credits — define basic uptime targets and credit mechanics; avoid open-ended service level promises.
5) Termination for convenience — limit to 30 days' notice and ensure refund logic for pre-paid usage.
6) Security evidence — provide SOC 2 link (see below) and make minimal DPA edits.

Target: legal will produce tracked changes and a short negotiation memo by COB Aug 24. If the vendor has materially shifted core commercial terms in their first pass, tag me and we'll request a short call with their lead counsel.

SOC2 artifact: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3cSOC2Report

Thanks —
Laura Bennett
Head of Contracts & Commercial Legal
laura_bennett@redwood.com
